analysis:
This batch is documentation only. Units 9bceb6d953b336e2:12/13 show head lines 1644-2222 of docs/architecture/inference.md. They are unchanged surrounding text; the actual change is at head 595-611 (patch excerpt only). That change documents a Gated DeltaNet four-row prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. The kernel is probed once per process and instantiation, and is kept only when it is bit-exact with gated_delta_step on the GPU; otherwise the stock kernel runs. configuration.md head 414 adds the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED environment variable (off/packed/rows/probe). Forced kernels skip the bit-exactness check and are described as A/B measurement only; the variable is read once and not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

Security relevance: this is a numerical/performance knob under operator control (TB-003/ADV-001). An operator can already alter outputs (T-007, T-012, T-013), so a forced inexact kernel adds no new trust escalation. The doc claims that mixing kernels preserves the recurrent state used by complete-checkpoint prefix capture (T-041). If a forced non-bit-exact kernel populated SSD prefix checkpoints, cached state could diverge for later same-scope requests. However, cache entries are bound to the account/model/contract scope and the operator can already corrupt outputs, so cross-tenant exposure is unchanged.

The GatedDelta.swift source is not supplied, so the probe correctness, the env parsing, and whether forced mode is reachable in production serving remain unverified. No changes were seen to crypto, attestation, authorization, billing or the cache name derivation, and no regression was identified.
